sections.title: Research 01 — Qatar regulation, QCB rules and QIB public facts

items.title: Researched 7 October 2026 for the QIB pre-approval remediation platform (Jahiz). Method: web search and fetch of primary pages where reachable. Every claim carries its source. Items marked UNVERIFIED could not be confirmed against a primary text.
Access limitation
items.body: The primary regulator domains qcb.gov.qa (Instructions to Banks PDFs, Customer Protection Department page, Data Handling Regulation PDF), almeezan.qa (official law texts) and qfiu.gov.qa (QCB AML/CFT Instructions May 2020) could not be fetched from the research environment. The Qatar Credit Bureau site (cb.gov.qa) was partly reachable. Where a QCB rule is cited below it is via secondary sources (law-firm notes, Oxford Business Group, bank product pages that restate the rule, HSBC Qatar's account disclosures). The exact QCB circular text should be pulled directly before any client-facing use of these figures.

sections.title: Research 01 · QCB rules on personal finance / consumer loans to individuals

items.title: Origin and date. The retail lending limits in force today trace to a QCB directive issued in April 2011 (Lexology dates it 10 April 2011).
items.body: It fixed caps on amount, tenor, instalment-to-salary ratio and pricing, and prohibited the buying and selling of personal loans between banks. Circular number: not given in any reachable source. Sources: https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=d0aed7fc-7335-48b1-a4b6-c48ab5e0f16a; https://oxfordbusinessgroup.com/reports/qatar/2012-report/economy/all-change-separation-of-islamic-finance-and-credit-restrictions-head-the-recent-adjustments-to-the-system

items.title: Maximum amounts. Qatari nationals
items.body: QAR 2,000,000. Non-Qataris: QAR 400,000. Banks restate these as the cap "including profit/interest", i.e. the cap applies to the total repayable: QIB (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/type/personal-finance), Ahlibank (https://ahlibank.com.qa/en/borrow/personal-loan), Commercial Bank (https://www.cbq.com.qa/en/personal/loans/personal-loan/personal-loan-against-salary-transfer/new-loan), QNB (https://www.qnb.com/sites/qnb/qnbqatar/page/en/enpersonalloansqataris.html, https://www.qnb.com/sites/qnb/qnbqatar/page/en/enpersonalloansexpats.html).

items.title: Maximum tenor. Qataris 72 months; expatriates 48 months. Sources
items.body: Lexology, OBG, and the QIB/Ahlibank/CBQ/QNB pages above. QIB vehicle finance also shows "up to 72 months" (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/type/vehicle-finance).

items.title: Instalment cap (debt burden ratio) and its base.
items.body: The 2011 directive set the monthly instalment ceiling at 75% of salary for Qataris and 50% for non-Qataris. Banks state the base as: Qataris "75% of basic salary + social allowance", expatriates "50% of total salary" — identical wording at QIB (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/type/personal-finance) and Ahlibank (https://ahlibank.com.qa/en/borrow/personal-loan), which indicates a regulatory formula rather than bank policy. The same 75%/50% DBR appears in the July 2023 QCB mortgage amendments (https://marhaba.qa/loans-bank-charges-and-interest-rates-in-qatar/; https://www.qna.org.qa/en/News-Area/News/2023-07/08/0020-qatar-central-bank-amends-mortgage-regulations). Whether the QCB text itself says "basic salary + social allowance": UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Treatment of existing commitments / standing orders.
items.body: No reachable source states the QCB rule on whether standing orders count toward the 75%/50%. Banks require a "liability letter from existing bank + 6 months bank statements" for buy-outs (QIB page above), and the Qatar Credit Bureau gives banks "customers' total exposure in the market and the loans they hold" (https://marhaba.qa/qatar-central-bank/). UNVERIFIED whether non-bank standing orders (rent, school fees) are counted; Gulf-bank practice is to count bureau-reported instalments and card minimums.

items.title: Pricing cap. OBG
items.body: maximum rate "the QCB lending rate plus 1.5 percentage points" (2011). Lexology: "maximum interest rate of 6.5 per cent". Marhaba.qa repeats 6.5% and lists the QCB lending rate as 4.35% (April 2026). Whether the +1.5pp formula still governs: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Credit cards (2011 directive).
items.body: Card limit capped at "double net total salary"; maximum interest 1% per month; cards issued without salary assignment non-renewable at expiry (OBG). Lexis Middle East, 13 April 2011: "Qatar: No Credit Card Without Salary Transfer: QCB" (https://www.lexismiddleeast.com/news/2011-04-13_28/en).

items.title: Salary transfer. No reachable QCB text mandates salary transfer for personal loans, but every Qatari bank product page requires salary assignment to the lending bank: Ahlibank,…
items.body: Salary transfer. No reachable QCB text mandates salary transfer for personal loans, but every Qatari bank product page requires salary assignment to the lending bank: Ahlibank, CBQ ("Salary Transfer Letter"), Dukhan Bank (https://www.dukhanbank.com/useful-tools/faqs), QIB ("salary credited to QIB account" for Instant Finance, https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/benefits/financing-benefits/instant-finance). For expatriates, banks also take an end-of-service assignment and post-dated security cheques (Ahlibank). Marhaba.qa: "No post-dated cheques permitted for loan collateral" for Qataris.

items.title: Age limits. No QCB text reachable. QIB
items.body: Qataris 18–65, residents 21–60 (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/type/personal-finance); Ahlibank: Qataris 18 at application / 70 at maturity, expatriates 21 / 60 at maturity. The expatriate 60-at-maturity figure is consistent across banks; whether it is a QCB rule: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: 2019–2026 amendments.
items.body: Only the July 2023 real-estate finance amendment was found. In April 2016 QCB publicly denied reports of tightened personal-loan rules (https://www.gulf-times.com/story/487658/Central-bank-denies-personal-loan-curbs). No evidence of a change to the QAR 2m/400k, 72/48 month or 75%/50% parameters since 2011.

sections.title: Research 01 · QCB customer protection / conduct rules

items.title: QCB has a Customer Protection Department (https://www.qcb.gov.qa/en/pages/customer-protection-department.aspx; content not retrievable).
items.body: QCB can fine banks up to QAR 10 million for breaches; a March 2014 directive required banks to answer customer-care calls and resolve complaints promptly, no day-count given (https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/02/03/2014/qcb-warns-banks-on-customers-complaints). Complaint time limits, notice periods, Arabic-language requirement, collection-conduct rules, contact hours: UNVERIFIED (no QCB text reachable). Bank tariffs state charges are "subject to change without prior notice, provided that the Bank shall comply with Qatar Central Bank's instructions" (https://www.cbq.com.qa/-/media/project/cbq/cbqwebsite/documents/tarrif-of-charges/cbq-personal-banking-tarrif-of-charges-en.pdf). A debt-collection vendor blog claims QCB guidelines prohibit harassment and inconvenient-hours contact but is unsourced (https://www.debt-works.com/consumer-debt-collection-in-qatar-best-practices-and-legal-considerations/) — UNVERIFIED.

items.title: QCB Data Handling and Protection Regulation (February 2025).
items.body: Issued 16–17 February 2025, applies to QCB-licensed institutions and fintechs; covers data governance, customer protection, data security, business continuity. Vendor summaries describe explicit consent before data is collected, processed, shared or retained (except where legally/contractually required), separate consent for marketing, purpose limitation, a retention policy with deletion rights, and third-party checks before sharing. Sources: https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/17/02/2025/qcb-issues-data-handling-and-protection-regulation; https://www.mondaq.com/financial-services/1590298/the-qatar-central-bank-issues-data-handling-and-protection-regulations; https://securiti.ai/solutions/qatar-central-bank-data-handling-and-protection-regulation/. Primary PDF not reachable; specifics UNVERIFIED against the text.

sections.title: Research 01 · Personal data law (Law 13 of 2016), NCGAA guidance, and CRA rules on unsolicited messages

items.title: Law No. 13 of 2016 (PDPPL). Art. 22
items.body: electronic communications for direct marketing are forbidden "except after obtaining the prior consent" of the individual; the message must identify the sender, state that it is marketing, and give an easily reachable address to request cessation. Art. 10: no retention beyond the necessary period; accuracy and relevance. Art. 5: consent withdrawable at any time. Art. 16: data "of a special nature" needs permission from the competent department. Arts. 23–24: fines up to QAR 1 million (Arts. 4, 8–12, 14–15, 22) and QAR 5 million (Arts. 13, 16, 17). English text: https://www.dataguidance.com/sites/default/files/law_no._13_of_2016_on_protecting_personal_data_privacy_-_english.pdf; corroborated by https://www.sharqlawfirm.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Article-Data-Protection.pdf and https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?t=electronic-marketing&c=QA.

items.title: Regulator. Originally the Compliance and Data Protection Department of MoTC (guidelines December 2020); now the National Cyber Governance and Assurance Affairs (NCGAA) under the…
items.body: Regulator. Originally the Compliance and Data Protection Department of MoTC (guidelines December 2020); now the National Cyber Governance and Assurance Affairs (NCGAA) under the National Cyber Security Agency. Breach notification within 72 hours (InCountry summary; article reference UNVERIFIED). https://incountry.com/blog/qatar-data-protection-law-guide-for-global-companies/

items.title: NCSA guideline "Electronic Communications for Direct Marketing" (PDPPL-02050218E, Nov 2020, updated Sept 2022) exists…
items.body: NCSA guideline "Electronic Communications for Direct Marketing" (PDPPL-02050218E, Nov 2020, updated Sept 2022) exists (https://ncsa.gov.qa/shared/document_library/94787172324409/33000/8860/1.0~41288b9d-9fd0-474b-9e8c-7eca3eedf743) but its content could not be read. UNVERIFIED beyond existence.

items.title: ID copies. No Qatar-specific rule on retention of QID copies beyond Art.
items.body: 10's necessity principle and the 10-year AML record-keeping obligation. AML retention is the governing floor for KYC documents.

items.title: CRA Spam Regulation (amended 6 August 2017). Art. 6(2)(c)
items.body: no direct marketing without prior consent. Art. 6(2)(d): "No Direct Marketing shall be sent between the hours of 21:00 and 09:00." Art. 6(3): withdrawal of consent effective within two business days; SMS/MMS must carry a free, functional unsubscribe. Art. 6(4): sender identification in Arabic and English, valid for at least 30 days. Consent presumed where an existing relationship exists and the message is relevant to it, with easy opt-out (e-Commerce Law Art. 54(b)). Art. 8(e): breaches may be referred to the Public Prosecutor. Source: https://www.cra.gov.qa/-/media/System/1/A/1/B/1A1B31855B7654C4A360A3C20E55D739/Spam-Regulation-Amended-English-Version.ashx. Vendor guide (8am–9pm, OTP exempt): https://www.sent.dm/en/resources/sms-compliance/qatar-sms-guide; the CRA text is the authority.

items.title: Design implication
items.body: a remediation message ("your QID has expired, update it to keep your offer") is a service message tied to an existing relationship, but it must carry sender identity and opt-out and should respect the 09:00–21:00 window.

sections.title: Research 01 · Qatar Credit Bureau and bounced cheques

items.title: Bureau. Established under QCB Decision No.
items.body: 5 of 2008; operational since 2011 (https://marhaba.qa/qatar-central-bank/; https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/25/03/2021/Qatar-Credit-Bureau-launches-new-service-providing-credit-reports-online). Members: banks, financial institutions, finance companies; Ooredoo and Vodafone Qatar joined February 2016. About 370,000 reports a year to members (322,000 on individuals). Operates under QCB (https://www.cb.gov.qa/English/Services/Pages/becomemember.aspx).

items.title: What it reports. Credit facilities from any provider, a summary of overall credit standing, dishonoured cheques (https://www.cb.gov.qa/English/Services/Pages/ourservices.aspx).
items.body: It cannot grant credit or impose restrictions on banks (marhaba.qa).

items.title: Credit score. A "Credit Scoring" product exists (https://www.cb.gov.qa/English/Pages/default.aspx).
items.body: Score range and bands: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Consent. "No entity can access your credit report without your prior consent." Consent via SMS reply, the bureau app, or the e-services portal, behind the National Authentication…
items.body: Consent. "No entity can access your credit report without your prior consent." Consent via SMS reply, the bureau app, or the e-services portal, behind the National Authentication System (https://www.cb.gov.qa/English/Services/Pages/Electronic-Consent-Service.aspx). Implication: a pre-approval engine needs a standing or in-journey consent step for bureau inquiries.

items.title: Retention — dishonoured cheques.
items.body: Kept "for a period of three years from the date of the cheque settlement"; no new cheque books until dishonoured amounts are paid; status updates to "paid" once settled (https://www.cb.gov.qa/English/Services/Pages/Bouncedchequereport.aspx). Retention for loan defaults: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Bounced cheques — criminal position. Penal Code (Law 11 of 2004) Art. 357
items.body: imprisonment three months to three years and/or fine QAR 3,000–10,000 (https://www.raya.com/2026/09/03/تعزيز-الوعي-القانوني-يقلل-الشيكات-المرتجعة; https://www.business.hsbc.com.qa/-/media/library/markets-selective/qatar/pdf/download-centre/qatar-account-disclosures-english.pdf; https://www.gulf-times.com/story/413572/penalties-for-a-bounced-cheque). Art. 358: penalty may be dropped or suspended on settlement at any stage. 2019: cheque-book withdrawal and a blacklist of habitual offenders; 37,130 cheque cases filed in 2018 (https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/05/08/2019/New-procedures-to-deter-bounced-cheques).

items.title: 2022–2026 changes. Law No.
items.body: 1 of 2024 (effective 6 April 2024) replaced Art. 585 of the Commercial Law: mandatory partial payment of the available balance, annotation, certificate of partial payment; criminal liability unchanged (https://qatarlaw.com/article/a-new-commercial-law-amendment-regarding-cheques; https://www.tasshamjit.com/qatar-introduces-cheque-payment-reforms-key-amendments-to-commercial-law/). Al Raya (Sept 2026): QCB measures include transaction-history review before issuing cheque books, a central returned-cheque database, listing in credit reports, no new cheque books until full payment, QAR 500 administrative fee per returned cheque; beneficiaries have 30 days to file a criminal complaint. HSBC Qatar's disclosures confirm listing in the bounced-cheques report and possible account closure for repeat returns.

sections.title: Research 01 · "Cautionary note" / caution flags in Gulf core banking systems

items.title: No Qatar-specific public taxonomy found.
items.body: UNVERIFIED as a QCB category list. Supporting sources:

items.title: Core systems implement these as posting restrictions or fund blocks set by the bank or third parties (courts, regulators); Temenos names death, creditor judgments,…
items.body: Core systems implement these as posting restrictions or fund blocks set by the bank or third parties (courts, regulators); Temenos names death, creditor judgments, payment/clearing holds and disputes (https://developer.temenos.com/article/end-end-account-services-workflow).

items.title: Court attachment/freeze under Judicial Enforcement Law No. 4 of 2024
items.body: electronic identification of bank assets (Art. 100); freezing orders (Art. 102); salary attachment capped at 25% of net monthly income (Art. 57); travel bans (Art. 36); automatic cancellation on full satisfaction with a discharge certificate (Art. 37) (https://practiceguides.chambers.com/practice-guides/enforcement-of-judgments-2026/qatar).

items.title: Sanctions: Public Prosecutor Decision No. 1 of 2020
items.body: freeze within 12 hours (domestic) / 24 hours (UN), release within three business days of delisting (https://www.sc.com/qa/uploads/sites/39/content/docs/Decision-No.-1-of-2020-Regulating-the-Implementation-Mechanisms-EN.pdf). QIB screens against Qatar, UN, UK HMT, EU and US lists (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/sustainability/frameworks-and-policies/amlcft-position-statement).

items.title: Deceased
items.body: CBQ terms close the current account on death, incapacity, bankruptcy, insolvency or arrest (Clause 4(f)) (https://www.cbq.com.qa/-/media/project/cbq/cbqwebsite/documents/terms-and-conditions/cb-retail-terms-and-conditions-en.pdf).

items.title: Employment ended / salary stopped
items.body: CBQ documents a "Blocked" status triggered by an employer's termination notification or end-of-service payment and by an outstanding monthly payment; recovery requires a new QID, new employment details with salary certificate, and receipt of the first salary (https://www.cbq.com.qa/en/personal/ways-to-bank/account-recovery-guide). QNB's loan terms make the loan immediately due on change of employer, resignation or termination (https://www.qnb.com/sites/qnb/qnbqatar/document/en/PLTC).

items.title: KYC-expired
items.body: Gulf Bank (Kuwait) terms allow stopping transactions if the customer refuses regulatory documents, reactivating when the reason ends (https://www.e-gulfbank.com/media/1451d28cef56e38e649ce0eee6b75201.pdf).

items.title: Working taxonomy (UNVERIFIED as QIB's codes)
items.body: deceased; court attachment/freeze; sanctions/designation; fraud/AML investigation; legal hold; KYC/QID expired; salary stopped / employer termination notice; delinquency block; dormant. Only KYC-expired, salary-stopped, delinquency and dormant are customer-remediable.

sections.title: Research 01 · QIB specifically (public pages only)

items.title: One Click Finance / Instant Finance. Launched 28 November 2018 as "Instant Finance"
items.body: eligible (pre-approved) customers receive "an SMS and/or a notification through their QIB Mobile App", choose amount, confirm, e-sign and receive funds "within minutes" (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/about-us/media-center/news/news-listing/2018/11/28/qib-the-first-islamic-bank-in-the-world-to-introduce-instant-finance-through-the-app; https://www.gulf-times.com/story/614441/QIB-introduces-instant-finance-via-mobile-app). The Digital Banker: "Instant Finance (One Click Financing)... in 5 mins" (https://thedigitalbanker.com/qatar-islamic-bank-accelerating-digitisation-to-attract-new-customers/). November 2024: AI-based credit risk models "enable pre-approval for the award-winning One Click finance and instant credit card offerings"; the app has "over 280 features" (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/about-us/media-center/news/news-listing/2024/11/03/qib-expands-international-wallet-transfers-and-enhances-digital-aipowered-features-on-its-mobile-app). Instant Finance eligibility: salary credited to a QIB account; fixed-deposit holders (up to 100% against the deposit); existing finance customers for top-ups; four steps, no paperwork, app only (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/benefits/financing-benefits/instant-finance).

items.title: Digital share (2023).
items.body: 52% of retail sales through digital channels; 71% of new accounts opened digitally; 83% of retail customers digitally active (https://www.theasianbanker.com/updates-and-articles/qatar-islamic-bank-redefines-retail-banking-in-qatar-through-digital-innovation-customer-focus-and-sustainable-growth-2024).

items.title: Personal Finance product.
items.body: Qataris 18–65, residents 21–60; confirmed employment with a QIB-approved employer; instalment ≤ 75% of basic salary + social allowance (Qataris) or 50% of total salary (residents); minimum QAR 15,000; maximum QAR 2m / QAR 400k "including profit rate"; documents: salary certificate, valid QID (Qataris) or residency permit + passport (expats), liability letter + 6 months statements for buy-outs; same-day financing, grace period up to 3 months, Credit Shield Takaful, top-up, no processing fees (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/type/personal-finance). Shari'a structure not named on the page: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Vehicle Finance. Same age bands and DBR formula; Qataris no down payment, expats 20% minimum; tenor up to 72 months…
items.body: Vehicle Finance. Same age bands and DBR formula; Qataris no down payment, expats 20% minimum; tenor up to 72 months (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/financing/type/vehicle-finance). Other: Home Finance up to 240 months, Qard Hasan for retirees up to QAR 300,000.

items.title: Salary and employer conditions.
items.body: "Your employer must be a company listed with QIB for you to be eligible for special finance rates" (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/help-support/personal/accounts/new-to-qatar). "Your employer needs to be registered with QIB for salary transfers"; if not, QIB coordinates with HR/payroll (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/help-support/personal/accounts/switch-to-qib). QIB@work targets employees of government, semi-government or large private companies earning over QAR 5,000 (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/special-programs/qibwork/). Minimum salary for personal finance not stated: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Segments (names on qib.com.qa).
items.body: Private Banking (qualifying total relationship value not disclosed; by invitation/referral; centre at Al Sadd) (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/accounts/tiers/private-banking). Tamayuz Banking (QAR 350,000 average deposit for 6 months, or salary credit QAR 50,000/month, or non-salaried with financing ≥ QAR 3m and inflows ≥ QAR 1.5m/yr; dedicated RM and call centre) (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/accounts/tiers/tamayuz-banking). Essential Banking (entry tier) (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/accounts/tiers/essential-banking). QIB Lite app for low-income customers (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/about-us/media-center/news/news-listing/2025/05/14/qib-introduces-new-innovative-features-on-its-mobile-apps-to-enhance-customer-experience).

items.title: Channels. Mobile app (iOS, Android, Huawei), Internet Banking, SMS Banking, Zaki AI virtual assistant (website and app, Arabic/English; can update personal details and request…
items.body: Channels. Mobile app (iOS, Android, Huawei), Internet Banking, SMS Banking, Zaki AI virtual assistant (website and app, Arabic/English; can update personal details and request callbacks) (https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/07/11/2021/qib-introduces-new-features-to-its-ai-virtual-assistant-zaki), 24-hour phone lines, email info@qib.com.qa, web contact form with preferred contact time (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/about-us/contact-us). App supports QID/passport update (https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/27/07/2020/QIB-announces-new-features-to-its-award-winning-Mobile-App). Digital onboarding scans QID and passport, takes a selfie, uploads salary certificate (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/news/the-first-in-qatar-qib-enables-new-customers-to-open-a-current-account-and-transfer-their-salaries-through-the-qib-mobile-app/). WhatsApp banking: no QIB page found — UNVERIFIED / likely not offered.

items.title: KYC refresh notice on qib.com.qa.
items.body: "In compliance with the regulatory requirements... QIB regularly request you to update the information related to your account"; fields QID number, expiry date, RIM number; channels: app (Profile → My Personal Data), portal https://ibank.qib.com.qa/retail/en/kyc/validate-qid, branch; "Failing to comply with this requirement might unfortunately lead to closing your account" (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/update-retail-account-information/).

items.title: AML framework. QIB cites Law 20 of 2019 and QCB Circulars 17 and 18 of 2020; risk tiers prohibited/high/medium/low; records retained minimum 10 years…
items.body: AML framework. QIB cites Law 20 of 2019 and QCB Circulars 17 and 18 of 2020; risk tiers prohibited/high/medium/low; records retained minimum 10 years (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/sustainability/frameworks-and-policies/amlcft-position-statement).

sections.title: Research 01 · QID / passport expiry and bank records

items.title: QID validity. Qatari citizens
items.body: 10 years (5 for under-16s) (https://www.wikiprocedure.com/index.php/Qatar_-_Renew_Identity_(ID)_Card). Expatriate residence permits: MOI renews for "1 to 3 years" (https://hukoomi.gov.qa/en/services/renew-residence-permit-for-expatriates); 5-year categories reported by unofficial guides — UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Grace and fines. Law 21 of 2015 Art. 10(1)
items.body: RP procedures within 30 days of entry; fine QAR 10/day capped at QAR 6,000 by reconciliation, up to QAR 10,000 judicially (https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/08/07/2024/fine-up-to-qr10000-for-not-completing-residence-permit-procedures-reminds-moi). A 90-day post-expiry grace at QAR 10/day is stated by unofficial guides — UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Bank obligation to hold a valid QID. QNB
items.body: QID within 90 days of opening "otherwise the account will be blocked as per Qatar Central Bank policy" (https://www.qnb.com/sites/qnb/qnbqatar/page/en/encurrentaccountpage.html). Doha Bank: "If you do not update your information, some of your Banking services might be impacted" (https://www.dohabank.com.qa/customer-information-update/). CBQ: customers must inform the bank "immediately" of changes in legal, residential or employment status (Clause 23(b)). QNB loan terms: borrower must keep mobile and email current.

items.title: AML law basis. Law No. 20 of 2019
items.body: CDD on establishing a relationship, transactions ≥ QAR 50,000, suspicion, and "when doubts arise regarding previously collected customer data"; ongoing due diligence; records ≥ 10 years (https://www.addleshawgoddard.com/en/insights/insights-briefings/2020/corporate-crime--investigations-update/qatars-new-anti-money-laundering-law/; https://www.getfocal.ai/blog/anti-money-laundering-laws-in-qatar). QFCRA guidance: firms "should obtain updated CDD information (including updated copies of the customer's passport or identity documents if these have expired)"; review frequency follows risk rating (https://eforms.qfcra.com/PublishedFiles/AttachmentsToNotice/Notice_50/Guidance%20on%20Customer%20Due%20Diligence%20March%202020.pdf). QCB's own fixed refresh cycle: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: Standard documents banks request.
items.body: Salary certificate; valid QID; passport copy (expats); residence permit; salary transfer letter; end-of-service assignment and post-dated security cheques (expats); liability letter + 6 months statements for buy-outs; showroom quotation for vehicle finance.

sections.title: Research 01 · Dormant and "status not normal" accounts

items.title: Dormancy trigger. HSBC Qatar's QCB-governed disclosures
items.body: dormant after "one year for current accounts, and five years for term and call deposit accounts" with no transactions and no contact (HSBC PDF above). QCB instruction text: UNVERIFIED. Dormant-account fees uniform at QAR 10/month on balances under QAR 500 (CBQ, Dukhan, Ahlibank tariffs), suggesting a QCB fee cap (QCB document 13-141 exists, not reachable).

items.title: Non-normal statuses documented.
items.body: Blocked for employer termination notice / EOS payment; blocked for outstanding instalment (CBQ recovery guide). Closed on death, incapacity, bankruptcy, insolvency or arrest (CBQ T&Cs). Blocked for failure to present QID within 90 days (QNB) or to refresh KYC (QIB). Court attachment/freeze (JEL 2024). Sanctions freeze (Decision 1/2020). A QCB-defined enumeration: UNVERIFIED.

sections.title: Research 01 · "Approved employers" lists

items.title: No QCB rule or public criteria list found; bank-specific practice.
items.body: QIB requires employers to be "listed"/"registered" with QIB (section 6). QNB: same-day loans to "QNB salaried customer working for approved company". 2013 Gulf Times: government employees on a "prime list"; private-sector employers had to provide Commercial Registration and financial statements (https://www.gulf-times.com/story/366227/loan-applications-face-closer-scrutiny). Unofficial guides confirm employees of unlisted companies are often declined (https://www.closecareer.com/thinking-about-personal-loan-in-qatar-here-is-a-facts/). WPS salary payment through banks mandatory since 2015 (https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/10/08/2015/online-salary-payments-from-august-18); QIB offers WPS to employers (https://www.qib.com.qa/en/wholesale/corporate/wages-protection-system/). Whether WPS compliance, headcount or tenure are listing criteria: UNVERIFIED.

sections.title: Research 01 · Ten most load-bearing facts and confidence

items.title: QCB retail caps: QAR 2m / 72 months (Qataris), QAR 400k / 48 months (expatriates), including profit.
items.body: High.

items.title: Instalment cap: 75% of basic salary + social allowance (Qataris); 50% of total salary (expatriates).
items.body: High for percentages; medium-high for the base wording.

items.title: Credit Bureau reports need the customer's prior consent (SMS/app/portal); dishonoured-cheque records stay three years from settlement.
items.body: High.

items.title: Bounced cheques remain criminal (Art.
items.body: 357); Law 1/2024 mandatory partial payment; Art. 358 lapse on settlement. High.

items.title: Direct electronic marketing needs prior consent (PDPPL Art.
items.body: 22; CRA Art. 6(2)(c)); none 21:00–09:00; opt-out within two business days; existing-relationship messages presumed consented with opt-out. High.

items.title: Expired/missing QID leads to block/closure (QNB 90 days; QIB closure warning); AML Law 20/2019 CDD refresh and 10-year retention.
items.body: High for bank practice; medium for the QCB instruction.

items.title: Dormancy: one year (current), five years (term); QAR 10/month fee under QAR 500.
items.body: Medium.

items.title: QIB One Click/Instant Finance: AI pre-approval; eligibility = salary credited to QIB, or deposit holder, or existing finance customer; SMS/app notification; funds in minutes.
items.body: High.

items.title: QIB segments: Private Banking, Tamayuz (QAR 50k salary or QAR 350k deposits), Essential Banking.
items.body: High.

items.title: Court freezes lift on satisfaction with discharge certificate; salary attachment capped at 25%; sanctions freezes lift only on delisting.
items.body: High.

items.title: To obtain directly from QCB documents
items.body: Instructions to Banks consumer-credit chapter (age at maturity, standing orders, salary transfer); Credit Bureau chapter (default-record retention, mandatory inquiry); the 2025 Data Handling and Protection Regulation; Customer Protection complaint time limits; fee-cap circular 13-141.

sections.title: Research 02 — Outreach, KYC refresh, pre-approval and data-quality best practice (regulatory analogues)

items.title: Researched 7 October 2026 for the QIB pre-approval remediation platform (Jahiz). Every claim carries its source. Items marked UNVERIFIED could not be confirmed. Where a number is needed and no regulation supplies one, the parameter table at the end says "design default — no regulatory source".

sections.title: Research 02 · Contact frequency limits by regime

items.title: US — CFPB Regulation F (12 CFR 1006.14(b))
items.body: a collector is presumed compliant if it calls "neither (A) more than seven times within seven consecutive days; nor (B) within a period of seven consecutive days after having had a telephone conversation". https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1006/14/

items.title: Australia — ACCC/ASIC Debt Collection Guideline
items.body: maximum "3 phone calls a week or 10 a month"; hours weekdays 7:30am–9pm, weekends 9am–9pm; no contact on national public holidays; workplace contact only in working hours. https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/debt/what-debt-collectors-cant-do

items.title: Saudi Arabia — SAMA Debt Collection Regulations for Individual Customers (2018)
items.body: "The number of attempts to contact a consumer through their phone number must not exceed ten attempts within a period of 30 days." Channels: e-mail, registered mail, national address, SMS, phone. All calls recorded and kept ≥ 10 years; the customer is told the call is recorded; messages state the department's working hours. https://rulebook.sama.gov.sa/en/node/1696

items.title: UAE — CBUAE Consumer Protection Standards Art. 5, clause 5.2.5.6
items.body: collection contact only by e-mail, registered mail, courier, SMS, phone or a consented method; telephone attempts "must only be made during the hours of 9 AM to 8 PM"; no "unreasonable and excessive number of communication attempts"; no home/workplace visits without consent. 5.2.5.7: communications recorded and kept 5 years after settlement. https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/article-5-business-conduct

items.title: UK — FCA CONC 7.9.4R
items.body: no contact at unreasonable times; regard to reasonable requests (shift workers). No numeric cap; firms must have a documented, reasonable approach. CONC 7.3.4R: forbearance and due consideration. https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/conc7/conc7s9; https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/conc7/conc7s3; https://www.fdcapital.co.uk/conc-guide/

items.title: UK community-lender practice (Fair4All Finance 2025)
items.body: collections actions "should not be undertaken more than once a day" and within 9–5 unless the customer asks otherwise. https://fair4allfinance.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/RM11-Arrears-and-Collections-Strategy.pdf

sections.title: Research 02 · Permitted contact hours

items.title: US TCPA 47 CFR 64.1200(c)(1)
items.body: no solicitation before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. local time. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-64/subpart-L/section-64.1200 — Reg F 1006.6(b)(1): before 8:00 a.m. and after 9:00 p.m. presumed inconvenient. https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1006/6/ — stricter state windows exist (8–8, 9–6 etc.). https://activeprospect.com/blog/tcpa-calling-hours/

items.title: UAE — Cabinet Resolution No. 56 of 2024
items.body: marketing calls only 9:00am–6:00pm; explicit prior consent; Do Not Call Registry. https://www.mondaq.com/advertising-marketing-branding/1495836/new-telemarketing-regulations-introduced-in-uae — CBUAE draft telemarketing regulation for LFIs (2025, consultation): Mon–Fri 9am–6pm, Sat–Sun 12pm–5pm, none on official holidays; institution-level do-not-call list; board approval of campaigns. https://gulfnews.com/business/banking/uae-central-bank-plans-comprehensive-regulation-for-telemarketing-financial-products-and-services-1.500323886

sections.title: Research 02 · Do-not-contact / opt-out handling

items.title: Reg F 1006.6(c)(1)
items.body: written cease-communication request stops contact on that debt; 1006.6(e): every electronic message carries a clear, simple opt-out. TCPA: do-not-call requests honoured within "a reasonable time... not to exceed ten business days". CBUAE 5.1.1.9: consumers are opted out of promotional communication unless they opted in; 5.1.1.68(a): no repeated solicitation after opt-out; 5.1.1.10: LFIs "are prohibited from marketing loans/financing... through direct contact by telephone". CBUAE 6.1.3.4: expressed consent before direct marketing; consent records kept 5 years after the relationship ends. https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/node/4236

items.title: Design implication
items.body: a KYC/document-update request is a service or regulatory message, not marketing; marketing opt-outs should not suppress it. A pre-approved offer is marketing and must respect opt-in status. ICO guidance: a neutral regulatory communication with no promotion "is unlikely to count as direct marketing", the same content with promotional phrasing is. https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing/direct-marketing-and-regulatory-communications

sections.title: Research 02 · Channel consent — WhatsApp Business

items.title: Meta policy
items.body: contact only with the number and opt-in permission; free-form replies within 24 hours of the last user message, approved templates outside it; honour all opt-outs; low quality ratings throttle volume. https://business.whatsapp.com/policy; https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/overview/getting-opt-in; https://www.infobip.com/en/blog/how-to-collect-whatsapp-business-opt-ins — Emirates NBD reported 771 thousand WhatsApp Banking subscribers in 2024. https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/-/media/enbd/files/investor-relations/financial-information/presentations/emiratesnbd_investor_presentation_2025_q1.pdf

sections.title: Research 02 · Quiet periods

items.title: ACCC/ASIC
items.body: no contact on national public holidays, reduced weekend window. CBUAE draft: none on official holidays, shorter weekend window. Ramadan: UAE working hours reduced by 2 hours/day (Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022). https://gulfnews.com/uae/ramadan/ramadan-working-hours-in-uae-for-public-and-private-sectors-explained-1.500433650 — ADIB offered a one-month instalment deferral in Ramadan 2021. https://gulfnews.com/business/banking/ramadan-2021-abu-dhabi-islamic-bank-to-postpone-1-month-loan-installment-for-retail-clients-1.1618217063335 — UNVERIFIED: no published GCC regulator rule or bank policy sets specific Ramadan contact windows. Any Ramadan window is a design default.

sections.title: Research 02 · FATF baseline

items.title: Recommendation 10
items.body: ongoing due diligence; keep documents, data and information "up-to-date and relevant by undertaking reviews of existing records, particularly for higher-risk categories". https://cfatf-gafic.org/index.php/documents/fatf-40r/376-fatf- — Recommendation 11: CDD records kept ≥ 5 years after the relationship ends. https://cfatf-gafic.org/documents/fatf-40r/377-fatf-recommendation-11-record-keeping

sections.title: Research 02 · Risk-based refresh cycles

items.title: CBUAE CDD/KYC Guidance 3.4.1
items.body: annually (high), every two years (medium), every three years (low), plus event triggers (change of domicile/name, STR, blocked transactions, higher-risk product, employment change, outdated information, screening hits). https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/341-risk-based-periodic-and-event-driven-reviews

items.title: Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago (2025)
items.body: annually (high), 3 years (standard), 5 years (low); policies must state actions and timelines when documentation is not obtained. https://www.central-bank.org.tt/cbtt_storage/2025/04/guidance-for-periodic-reviews-april2025.pdf

items.title: FSC Mauritius (2026)
items.body: yearly / 3 years / 4 years; triggers include "expired or invalid identification materials". https://www.fscmauritius.org/media/ndycko0f/guidelines_frequency-of-cdd.pdf

items.title: RBI India: 2 / 8 / 10 years; low-risk may self-certify. https://factly.in/kyc-updation-low-risk-customers-must-done-every-10-years
SAMA: retail update frequency not fixed; updates allowed through electronic banking with reliable identity verification. https://rulebook.sama.gov.sa/node/1671
Wolfsberg (2022): move from periodic refresh toward trigger-based review. https://cbr.ru/Content/Document/File/139055/WG_G_DGL.PDF

sections.title: Research 02 · Expired identity documents — grace and restriction sequences

items.title: UAE — CBUAE 6.2.1.5
items.body: risk-based policy to update expired ID; after written notices and "a notice period of 90 calendar days", banks must temporarily block debit and credit cards (branch operations continue), no charges. https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/node/4236 — 2019 practice: SMS reminders, ID copies accepted via SMS, e-mail or RM. https://gulfnews.com/business/banking/some-uae-residents-credit-debit-cards-suspended-for-failing-to-update-emirates-id-details-banks-confirm-1.1553152666920 — In-app updates now standard. https://gulfnews.com/ask-gulf-news/ask-gulf-news-how-to-update-your-bank-kyc-in-the-uae-when-your-emirates-id-expires-1.500320726

items.title: Saudi — SAMA Rules for Bank Accounts: bank may freeze on ID expiry; must notify the freezing date ≥ 30 days in advance. https://rulebook.sama.gov.sa/en/node/1667
Kuwait (2018): one bank blocked immediately, five gave three months after expiry. https://kuwaittimes.com/update-your-contact-details-or-risk-having-account-blocked
Qatar — CBQ
items.body: non-response "will cause disruption or restrictions to services"; update via app or secure mail. https://www.cbq.com.qa/en/personal/know-your-customer — Banks send "multiple reminders" and may block, with extensions where passport renewal is delayed. https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/01/03/2021/Bank-customers-urged-to-update-documents-on-record

items.title: India — RBI
items.body: notice of three months, reminder for three more; partial freeze (credits allowed, debits blocked); full freeze after six further months. https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=9312 — RBI 2025: ≥ 3 advance intimations incl. one letter, ≥ 3 reminders after; low-risk individuals keep access one year after due. https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12866

sections.title: Research 02 · Request sequence

items.title: No regulator prescribes 90/60/30-day pre-expiry notices. Anchors
items.body: UAE 90-day written-notice period before card block; Saudi 30-day advance notice of freeze; India ≥ 3 pre and ≥ 3 post intimations. A T-90 / T-60 / T-30 / T0 / T+30 / T+60 cadence with card block at T+90 is a design default consistent with these.

sections.title: Research 02 · Acceptable in-app document update

items.title: UK GPG 45
items.body: strength, validity (genuineness, expiry, security features, MRZ, chip), activity, fraud, verification (biometric match with anti-spoofing at score 3). https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/identity-proofing-and-verification-of-an-individual/how-to-prove-and-verify-someones-identity — EBA remote onboarding guidelines (2022): reliable reproductions, consistent automated capture, liveness detection. https://www.walkersglobal.com/Insights/2022/12/EBA-Publishes-Guidelines-on-Remote--Customer-Onboarding — McKinsey: "Self-service should be the default option for customers providing KYC information." https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/banking-matters/making-your-kyc-remediation-efforts-risk-and-value-based

sections.title: Research 02 · Pre-approved / pre-screened credit offer practice

items.title: UAE — CBUAE Bank Loans Regulation (2011)
items.body: instalments ≤ 50% of gross salary; personal loan ≤ 20× salary; tenor ≤ 48 months. https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/sites/default/files/en_net_file_store/CBUAE_EN_3920_VER1.pdf — Consumer Protection Standards Art. 7: affordability, stress test with written summary, DBR compliance; 7.1.3.5(e): no automatic card limit increase without expressed consent and an updated bureau check. https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/node/4237

items.title: Saudi — SAMA Responsible Lending Principles
items.body: salary-linked obligations ≤ 33.33% of gross salary (25% retirees); non-mortgage ≤ 45%; total ≤ 55%/65% by income band; salary verified via the employer; other income via two-year statements. https://rulebook.sama.gov.sa/node/1971

items.title: Bank rules
items.body: ADCB — minimum salary AED 5,000, mandatory salary and gratuity transfer, listed employer, age 21+. https://adcb.com/en/get-in-touch/faqs/loans/personal-loan — Emirates NBD T&Cs: transferring salary elsewhere without approval is an event of default. https://Emiratesnbd.com/-/media/enbd/files/loan/personal-loan/personal-loans-tc.pdf — DIB: customer must inform the bank of employer change. https://www.dib.ae/docs/default-source/cpr/warning/liabilities-warnings-en-ar-sia.pdf

items.title: Missing or irregular salary month
items.body: no regulatory rule. Practitioner guidance: review 2–3 months minimum; credits traceable to the employer, consistent date; gaps may be innocent (bonus month, job change, delayed payroll); repeated gaps or non-matching source are red flags (vendor source). https://precisa.in/blog/how-to-analyse-salary-credits-bank-statements/ — US mortgage analogues: FHA six-month gap rule; Fannie Mae three-year continuance. https://mortgageguidelines.com/fha-job-gap-history-of-employment/; https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-3.1-01/general-income-information — Minimum continuous months and salary-variance tolerance: design defaults.

items.title: US FCRA prescreen
items.body: firm offers; opt-out five years or permanent; short and long notices. https://www.transunion.com/prescreen-opt-out; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-642

items.title: EU CCD2 (2023/2225)
items.body: Art. 17 prohibits credit "without their prior request and explicit agreement"; Art. 18 creditworthiness on verified information, human intervention and explanation where automated; application 20 Nov 2026. https://lawplayer.com/eu/article/32023L2225/art_17; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023L2225

items.title: Published eligibility/conversion statistics for pre-approved digital loans
items.body: none found. McKinsey mentions one bank whose "conversion rates tripled" after pre-approved top-ups and drop-offs cut "by up to 40 percent", no base rates. https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/banking-matters/ten-lessons-for-building-a-winning-retail-and-small-business-digital-lending-franchise — UNVERIFIED / not publicly available; do not cite a conversion figure.

sections.title: Research 02 · Data quality monitoring for customer master data

items.title: DAMA UK six dimensions
items.body: accuracy, completeness, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness, validity. https://www.gov.uk/government/news/meet-the-data-quality-dimensions — ISO/IEC 25012 adds currentness, compliance, traceability. https://quality.arc42.org/standards/iso-iec-25012 — BCBS 239 Principles 3–6. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BCBS_239

items.title: Mapping for this platform (design)
items.body: expired ID = validity/currentness; missing salary credit = completeness/timeliness; unapproved employer = compliance against a reference list; name mismatch = consistency; duplicate customer = uniqueness.

items.title: Remediation metrics
items.body: no regulator benchmarks. McKinsey: 20% more KYC automation cut outreaches per case 18% and raised throughput 48%; one bank cut customer contacts ~40%. https://www.mckinsey.com/business-functions/risk-and-resilience/our-insights/five-actions-to-build-next-generation-know-your-customer-capabilities — Suggested KPI set (design default): contact rate, response rate, cure rate, time-to-cure, re-fallout rate (12 months), escalation rate, complaints per 1,000 contacts.

sections.title: Research 02 · Email and document intake automation

items.title: MRZ check digits: ICAO 9303 weights 7-3-1 modulo 10. https://scanbot.io/blog/what-is-a-check-digit — Validity checks per GPG 45 (above).
items.body: EBA remote onboarding (above).

items.title: Human-in-the-loop thresholds (vendor guidance, to be calibrated)
items.body: identity fields 0.90–0.95; financial fields 0.95–0.98; compliance fields 0.97–0.99 or mandatory review; random audit of 5% of auto-approved documents; log "what changed, who changed it, when, and why"; leaked-error target < 0.5%. https://parseur.com/blog/hitl-best-practices

items.title: Audit and retention
items.body: FATF R.11 ≥ 5 years; CBUAE 6.1.6.1 ≥ 5 years, 5.2.5.7 collection communications 5 years; SAMA call recordings ≥ 10 years. Audit record content (NIST SP 800-53 AU-3): event type, when, where, source, outcome, identity. https://www.tarleton.edu/security-controls-catalog/audit-and-accountability-au/au-3-content-of-audit-records/ — ISO 27001:2022 A.8.15: log activities, privileged actions, exceptions, configuration changes; separate access-controlled log store. https://www.tcsa.in/frameworks/iso-27001/controls/8-15-logging

items.title: Inbound email practice
items.body: UAE banks accepted ID copies by SMS, e-mail or RM (2019); CBQ routes documents through in-app secure mail. An emailed document is lower-assurance evidence than an in-app capture with liveness and should require human verification before the record changes.

sections.title: Research 02 · Segment-based service models

items.title: Published GCC thresholds
items.body: QNB First — salary ≥ QAR 35,000 or ADB ≥ QAR 350,000; QNB First Plus — salary ≥ QAR 100,000 or ADB ≥ QAR 4m; Private by invitation. https://qnb.com/sites/qnb/qnbqatar/page/en/enaboutliferewards.html — QIB Private Banking: relationship value not published; by invitation or referral. https://www.qib.com.qa/en/personal/accounts/tiers/private-banking — Emirates NBD Private: USD 5m AUM. https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/priority-banking — Mashreq Gold: salary ≥ AED 80,000 or balance AED 500,000. https://mashreq.com/en/uae/gold/become-a-customer — ADCB Privilege: net salary ≥ AED 40,000 or balance ≥ AED 200,000. https://www.adcb.com/en/personal/adcb-for-you/segments/privilege/ — Standard Chartered Priority UAE: salary ≥ AED 30,000 or AED 370,000 funded. https://sc.com/ae/priority/eligibility-criteria/

items.title: Contact differentiation
items.body: Capgemini — HNWIs expect a dedicated RM reachable by meeting, phone, e-mail or secure messaging; ultra-HNWIs expect dedicated lines. https://www.capgemini.com/insights/research-library/wealth-advising-2024-key-trends-for-success/ — UNVERIFIED: no regulator rule routing HNWI communications via the RM; RM-first is a design default supported by the service models above.

sections.title: Research 02 · Human-in-the-loop and agent governance

items.title: CBUAE Guidance Note on responsible AI in the financial sector (February 2026, non-binding)
items.body: AI inventory; human in the loop / on the loop / out of the loop (the last only for "low-risk, non-material processes"); disclosures in Arabic and English for high-impact decisions; right to human review, challenge and correction. https://www.pinsentmasons.com/out-law/news/uae-central-bank-responsible-ai-guidance-financial-sector; https://www.centralbank.ae/media/mykn5fue/cbuae-issues-guidance-note-to-protect-consumers-and-ensure-responsible-use-of-artificial-intelligence-in-the-financial-sector-en.pdf — EU AI Act Art. 14 (override, automation-bias awareness) and Art. 12 (automatic logging). https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/14/; https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/12/ — GDPR Art. 22(3). https://gdpr-info.eu/art-22-gdpr/

items.title: Separation of duties
items.body: BCBS operational-risk principles (2021) paras 50–51 on dual controls; maker-checker / four-eyes. https://www.bis.org/bcbs/publ/d515.pdf; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maker-checker

items.title: Recommended approval matrix (design default)
items.body: no approval for templated reminders within policy, contact logging, scheduling; maker-checker before writing a KYC field from a document, lifting a block, changing contact details, marking a case cured; human-in-the-loop mandatory for anything with credit effect, for any VVIP/HNWI contact, and for hardship or complaint replies. Every agent action logged with who/what/when/where/outcome/evidence.

sections.title: Research 02 · Collections-adjacent reasons

items.title: FCA TR16/10
items.body: poor practice = refusing to change call times, payment-only focus; good practice = establishing circumstances. https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/impact-assessments/early-arrears-management-in-unsecured-lending-tr16-10.pdf — Fair4All example cadence: pre-due nudge; day 1 text and e-mail; day 4 reminder; day 7 first call; day 10 letter; one action per day; non-threatening language. — CONC 6.7.2R: monitor repayment record and act on signs of difficulty. https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/conc6/conc6s7 — CBUAE 5.1.2.10: monitor borrowers facing difficulty. https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/entiresection/44 — Self-cure statistics: UNVERIFIED.

items.title: No offers to customers in arrears
items.body: CONC 6.7.7R (no limit increase where at risk of financial difficulty); CONC 5.2A.22G; CCD2 Arts. 17–18, 35; CBUAE 7.1.2.3 and 7.1.3.5(e); 5.1.1.10. Design rule: suppress pre-approved offers for DPD > 0, returned cheque in the last 12 months, DBR breach, or an open hardship flag; the thresholds are design defaults.

sections.title: Research 02 · Recommended default parameters for the outreach policy (per segment)

items.title: Applies to service/regulatory outreach (document refresh, data correction).
items.body: Offer-related contact is additionally gated by opt-in status.

items.title: Max contacts per week (all channels, per customer)
items.body: Mass: 3 · High Value: 2 · HNWI: 1 (RM-initiated) · VVIP: 1 per 2 weeks, RM only · Source / basis: ACCC/ASIC 3 calls/week; SAMA ≤ 10 attempts/30 days; Reg F 7-in-7 upper bound; step-downs design default

items.title: Max per day
items.body: Mass: 1 · High Value: 1 · HNWI: 1 · VVIP: 1 · Source / basis: Fair4All "not more than once a day"; US state 3/24h caps

items.title: Max reminders per request
items.body: Mass: 3 before due + 3 after, incl. one letter/registered channel · High Value: 3 total, then RM · HNWI: 2 digital, then RM · VVIP: 1 courtesy notice, then RM · Source / basis: RBI ≥ 3 + ≥ 3 incl. letter; CBUAE written notices over 90 days; variants design default

items.title: Days between reminders
items.body: Mass: 30 (T-90, T-60, T-30), then 30, 30; block at T+90 · High Value: 30 · HNWI: 14, then RM · VVIP: RM discretion · Source / basis: CBUAE 90 days before card block; SAMA ≥ 30 days before freeze; intervals design default

items.title: Contact window (local)
items.body: Mass: 09:00–20:00 service; 09:00–18:00 for any call carrying an offer · High Value: same · HNWI: 09:00–18:00 RM hours · VVIP: agreed with client · Source / basis: CBUAE 9 AM–8 PM; UAE Cabinet Res. 56/2024 9–6; CRA Qatar no marketing 21:00–09:00

items.title: Channels allowed
items.body: Mass: App push, SMS, e-mail, WhatsApp (opt-in, templates), call after digital attempts · High Value: App push, e-mail, WhatsApp (opt-in), RM call · HNWI: RM call, secure in-app message, e-mail; no bulk SMS · VVIP: RM call/meeting; letter; no automated messages · Source / basis: CBUAE approved methods; WhatsApp policy; SAMA channel list; HNWI/VVIP limits design default

items.title: Escalate to human after N unanswered automated attempts
items.body: Mass: 3 · High Value: 2 · HNWI: 0 (RM first) · VVIP: 0 (RM only) · Source / basis: design default; CBUAE AI note allows out-of-loop only for low-risk steps

items.title: Quiet days / periods
items.body: Mass: Friday 11:30–14:00, public holidays, Eid; Ramadan 10:00–16:00, none 1h around iftar · High Value: same · HNWI: same · VVIP: same · Source / basis: ASIC/CBUAE draft on holidays; Ramadan windows design default — UNVERIFIED

items.title: Opt-out handling
items.body: Mass: Marketing opt-out within 10 business days (TCPA) / 2 business days (CRA Qatar); service messages continue via one neutral channel · High Value: same · HNWI: same · VVIP: same · Source / basis: TCPA; CRA Art. 6(3); CBUAE opt-out default; ICO service vs marketing

items.title: Restriction after non-response (expired ID)
items.body: Mass: T+90 temporary card block, branch operations allowed, no fee; hard block after a further notice · High Value: same, RM informed · HNWI: RM confirms before any block · VVIP: RM/segment head approval · Source / basis: CBUAE 6.2.1.5; RBI partial-then-full freeze

items.title: Offer suppression
items.body: Mass: No offer if DPD > 0, returned cheque in 12 months, DBR breach, hardship flag, opted out · High Value: same · HNWI: same · VVIP: same · Source / basis: CONC 6.7.7R; CBUAE 7.1.2.3, 7.1.3.5(e); CCD2 Art. 17; 12-month lookback design default

items.body: Mass: 5 years after settlement/relationship end (10 years for call recordings under SAMA; 10 years for KYC under Qatar AML law) · High Value: same · HNWI: same · VVIP: same · Source / basis: CBUAE 5.2.5.7, 6.1.6.1; SAMA; FATF R.11; Qatar Law 20/2019
